query: Single-phase ZrB2 benefits from strong Zr–B and B–B interactions and a high melting point, but it requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and does not readily meet application requirements on its own. Earlier studies sought to lower the required temperature, yet the resulting materials remained vulnerable to high-temperature oxidation or liquid plating-metal corrosion, while reported preparation temperatures generally remained above 1700 °C. Under the constraints of lower-temperature manufacture, adequate strength and structural integrity, oxidation durability, and prolonged service in a liquid plating bath, what single intervention could overcome these limitations? Provide one hypothesis specifying the intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome compared with single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens, applicable preparation and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment evaluating final body quality, structural integrity, oxidation, and liquid-metal corrosion that would falsify the hypothesis if its predictions were not observed.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating 10 vol% SiC whiskers into ZrB₂ powder and sintering by spark plasma sintering at 1 500 °C will enable full densification via transient B₂O₃–SiO₂ liquid‐phase sintering and, in service, the SiC whiskers will form a protective SiO₂ scale and bridge cracks, yielding higher toughness, lower oxidation rate, and superior resistance to molten‐metal corrosion compared with single‐phase ZrB₂ prepared either at 2 300 °C or at ≥1 700 °C.
generation.intervention: Addition of 10 vol% SiC whiskers; spark plasma sintering at 1 500 °C, 50 MPa, 10 min
generation.conditions: Sintering T: 1 400–1 600 °C; service in air up to 1 600 °C; exposure to molten aluminum at 700–750 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Interconnected network of SiC whiskers plus transient B₂O₃–SiO₂ liquid film at grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: Transient liquid‐phase sintering lowers the temperature needed for full densification; during high‐temperature exposure, SiC oxidizes to form a continuous SiO₂ barrier that slows further oxidation and blocks Al infiltration; SiC whiskers also bridge cracks to increase toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: ≥98 % of theoretical density; ≥30 % increase in fracture toughness; oxidation weight gain <2 mg/cm² after 100 h at 1 500 °C in air; mass loss <1 % after 100 h in molten Al at 700 °C
generation.baseline: Pure ZrB₂ sintered at 2 300 °C: ~95 % density, baseline toughness, oxidation gain >5 mg/cm², mass loss >10 % under identical service
generation.boundary: Whisker content 8–12 vol %; sintering 1 400–1 600 °C; service T ≤1 600 °C; molten Al bath 700–750 °C
generation.uncertainty: Extent of liquid‐phase sintering enhancement and uniformity of the protective SiO₂ scale under molten‐metal exposure

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets: (1) pure ZrB₂ sintered at 2 300 °C and (2) ZrB₂ + 10 vol% SiC whiskers sintered at 1 500 °C under otherwise identical SPS parameters. Measure final density, indentation fracture toughness, oxidation weight gain after 100 h at 1 500 °C in air, and mass change after 100 h exposure to molten Al at 700 °C.
measurements: mass change (%) in molten Al bath
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the composite has <95 % density, <10 % toughness improvement, oxidation gain >4 mg/cm², or mass loss >5 % under the specified tests.
